description: A dramatic chart race showing how SPACs exploded into the global IPO market — then collapsed after a manic 2020–2021 boom and regulatory backlash.
youtube_description:
2006–2026: The SPAC Bubble — from niche vehicle to global phenomenon to cautionary tale.

In this video we race two stories: traditional IPOs — the backbone of public markets — versus SPAC IPOs, the blank‑check companies that exploded in 2020–2021. SPACs were almost invisible for over a decade, then went from a few dozen a year to 613 IPOs in 2021 alone as investors chased fast routes to public markets. Big-name deals (DraftKings, Virgin Galactic, Lucid, Nikola and others) made headlines — then many deals disappointed, performance fell, lawsuits followed, and regulators stepped in. By 2022 the SPAC pipeline crashed, and the number of new SPAC listings tumbled back to a fraction of the peak.

What you’ll see in this chart race: a meteoric SPAC climb (and a brutal fall), set against the steadier, slower-moving traditional IPO market — which dipped in COVID 2020, surged in 2021, then normalized. This is a story about hype, liquidity, and how markets punish poor underwriting.

Like, subscribe, and hit the bell if you want more explosive timeline races. Tell us in the comments: which SPAC deal surprised or disappointed you the most?

Sources: Renaissance Capital, SEC filings, major market coverage (Bloomberg/WSJ/FT) and public IPO/SPAC trackers — data aggregated to count annual IPO listings and documented major SPAC milestones (2020–2023 regulatory actions and litigation).

Watch how the flashy SPAC line rockets past traditional IPOs… then falls back to earth. Would you have jumped on the ride?
